lignes: (A) A man is repairing a printer.

Who is in charge of the company website?
Please charge the battery first, before the call.
Ms. Kim from the marketing team manages it.
When does the new bus schedule take effect?
Starting the first of next month.
Yes, I take it to work every day.
The bus stop is across the street.
Have you updated your password yet?
The passenger lost his passport at the airport.
It's the second door on the right.
I'll do it right after this meeting.
Could you review the draft of our advertisement?
Our ads are mostly on social media.
Sure, send it over and I'll read it tonight.
The advertisement ran for two weeks last spring.
How much does a monthly train pass cost?
I pass by the station every day.
The train leaves at seven from the main station.
The new smartphone app is easier to use, isn't it?
Yes, the menus are much simpler now.
I'd like a larger conference room.
The app store opens at nine.
Where are we storing the video equipment?
A video of the product launch for our customers.
In the locked cabinet behind the studio.
Why was the flight to Boston delayed?
Yes, it was a very long flight.
There was a problem with the landing gear.
It's at gate twenty-three, near the main exit.
Would you like me to book your train tickets?
The ticket office is closed until nine tomorrow morning.
I read it on the train.
That would be great, I need to leave on Monday morning.
Didn't the printer stop working again?
A new printing plan for the brochure.
Yes, I'd like it done by noon.
No, the technician fixed it this morning.
What did the audience think of the commercial?
Most of them found it funny and memorable.
The commercial district is closed for the parade today.
I heard that the radio station is changing its format.
Yes, they're going to broadcast more news.
I changed my number last week.
The format of the report is fine.
Which software do you recommend for editing videos?
Some of the editors are working in Dubai this month.
The one our design team uses is quite easy.
If the shipment arrives late, who should we notify?
The ship leaves from Pier Nine on Thursday evening.
Call the client first, then update the manager.
How often does the shuttle run to the airport?
From the main terminal at six this evening.
Should I post the announcement on social media today?
Yes, there were three posts on our page today.
Wait until the legal team approves it.
Sam said the campaign budget was cut by half.
Half of the staff are waiting in the lobby for you.
That's a shame, we'll need to rethink our plans.
He cut the cake with a knife.
Is this the right platform for the Boston train?
Yes, the Boston office is bigger.
No, you need platform six, on the other side.
Let's launch the new ad campaign in March.
Yes, he marched down the street.
I think April would be safer, we need more time to test it.
Our lunch break begins at one, so let's talk about it after we eat.
How many followers does our page have now?
Just over twelve thousand, up from nine.
The page is on the left side of the screen, I think.
Do you want to take the express or the local train?
Yes, I left it on the train.
The express, if it isn't much more expensive.
I trained for two hours yesterday.
Who wrote the article about electric cars?
It's about two pages long, with two photographs.
I think it was Priya from the news desk.
Yes, the cars are parked outside.
We've run out of toner for the color printer.
The colors in this photo are beautiful.
No, I ran in the park this morning.
I'll order some from the supplier right away.
Please make sure the microphones are working before the broadcast.
He works at the television station downtown.
The broadcast channel is number nine.
I tested all of them an hour ago.
Can't we get a refund for the canceled train ticket?
Yes, I like traveling by train.
Only if we apply within thirty days.
The ticket line is shorter today than it was on Monday.
Is the new version of the accounting software ready? Everyone has been complaining that the old one freezes.
The update is installed on the test computers. It's much faster, but we found a problem with the report feature.
Will the vendor fix it before we roll it out?
They promised a patch by next Wednesday. I suggest we wait until then to install it on all computers.
Agreed. Let's tell the staff the switch will happen in two weeks instead.
I'll draft the email and send it to everyone this afternoon.
Our last email campaign only got a two percent response. I think we should try influencer videos this time.
Influencers are effective, but they're expensive. A cheaper option might be short clips of customer reviews.
That's true. We could offer a discount to customers who record a clip.
Good. How much of the budget are we planning to use?
Maybe a quarter. About six thousand dollars.
Fine. I'll ask the finance team to approve it today.
Tonight's interview with the mayor has been moved from seven to eight because of the city council vote.
That's fine, but I need time to review the questions. Could you send them to my tablet?
Already done. Also, the guest from the transport department can't make it, so we've invited a professor from the university instead.
A professor? That's a big change. What's the subject?
Traffic safety. She wrote a report on bicycle lanes last year.
Great. I'll read it before the show.
Hi, I'm trying to get to Manchester tomorrow morning. Is there a train before nine?
There's one at eight fifteen, but it's delayed because of track repairs, so it will leave at nine forty.
That's too late for my meeting. Is there another route?
You could take the express to Leeds and change there. It's faster, even though it costs ten pounds more.
I'll take that one. Can I pay by card?
Certainly. Your train leaves at seven forty from platform four.
Kevin, my laptop hasn't connected to the office network since this morning.
Twice. And I'm presenting to the sales team at eleven.
Rosa, if the laptop isn't fixed in time, you can borrow mine. I have the same presentation file in the cloud.
Mr. Cole, that's kind, but I'll bring Rosa a spare laptop in ten minutes. We'll look at hers after the presentation.
Thank you both. That's a relief.
The brochures just arrived from the printer, and the prices on page three are wrong.
Oh no. We only printed five hundred, right?
No, we printed two thousand. The printer says a reprint would cost nine hundred dollars.
Let's not reprint. We can put a sticker with the correct prices on each brochure.
That's cheaper, but it will take time. Can the interns help?
I'll ask them tomorrow. They're free after lunch.
I'm still waiting for a comment from the airport authority. Can I hand in the story tomorrow morning instead?
Our website needs to publish it tonight. Is there anyone else you can call?
I could call the airline spokesperson. She usually answers quickly.
Do that. And add a photo, the one from the press release is fine.
Okay. If the airline confirms the delay, should I mention the number of affected passengers?
Yes, as long as it's confirmed. Otherwise, leave it out.
The delivery to the Denver store is already two hours late. Carlos, what happened? Tom, you're on the line from the warehouse too.
A bridge on the highway is closed for repairs, so I had to take a longer route.
Yes, I'm here. If Carlos left at six, he should arrive by two. I'll tell the store manager.
Thanks. Carlos, please send me a message when you're thirty minutes away.
Will do. By the way, my truck's fuel gauge is acting strange.
Stop at the next station and have it checked. We can't risk another delay.
I bought this laptop two weeks ago, but the battery only lasts about two hours.
Have you installed the latest update? Sometimes that fixes battery problems.
Yes, I did it last night. It didn't help.
In that case, you can exchange it for another model or get a refund. We have a thirty-day return policy.
I'd like to exchange it. Is the model with the larger screen in stock?
We only have one left. Let me bring it from the back.
We start the live show in twenty minutes. Rita, are the guests here? And Dan, is the sound ready?
One of them is. The author is stuck in traffic, but she says she'll arrive by seven fifteen.
That's cutting it close, Rita. I need five minutes to test her microphone.
Then let's begin with the music segment and move the interview to the second half.
Good plan. I'll update the script.
And I'll set up the studio now.
Have you heard that the company is starting a carpool program next month?
Yes, I signed up already. Parking downtown costs me two hundred dollars a month.
Me too. I'd join if there were a driver in my neighborhood. I live near the lake.
I think Rebecca lives out there. She works in the legal department.
I'll send her a message. If she agrees, I could save about half of my commuting cost.
Then you could also use the express lane on the highway, which saves fifteen minutes.
Registrations for next week's webinar are lower than last time. We have only ninety so far.
Last time we had two hundred, but we emailed our entire customer list. This time we only posted online.
Then let's send an email tomorrow, and offer a free guide to everyone who attends.
Good idea. I can design the guide, but I'll need the content by Thursday.
I'll write it this week. Should we also ask the sales team to mention it to clients?
Yes, I'll bring it up at their meeting.
Hello, I'm checking in for the flight to Singapore, but the kiosk won't accept my booking number.
May I see your passport? I see the problem. Your reservation was made under a different spelling of your last name.
Oh, the travel agency must have made a typo.
No problem, I'll correct it. Do you have any luggage to check?
Just this suitcase. It's a little heavy, I'm afraid.
The limit is twenty-three kilograms, and yours is twenty-five. You'll need to pay an extra fee or remove a few items.

May I have your attention, please. The six twenty express to Glasgow has been canceled because of a signal failure near Carlisle. Passengers holding tickets for this train may board the six fifty local service, which will stop at all stations. Please note that it will arrive about forty minutes later than scheduled. To receive a full refund or a free coffee voucher, visit the customer service desk next to platform two. We apologize for the inconvenience.

Hi, Ms. Chen, this is Tony Rivera from Pixel Studio. I'm calling about the redesign of your online store. We've finished the home page, and I've emailed you the link so you can review it. There's one issue: the payment page loads slowly on mobile phones, so I'd like to ask our programmer to fix it before we go live. That might delay the launch from the first of June to the eighth. Could you call me back by tomorrow to let me know if that's acceptable?

Looking for something good to watch? Try StreamBox free for thirty days. With StreamBox, you can watch thousands of movies and television series on your phone, tablet, or television, and download programs to enjoy offline on long flights. Our new Family plan lets up to five people use one account, each with a personal profile. Sign up by Sunday, and your first three months will be half price. Download the StreamBox app today.

Good morning, everyone, and welcome to this briefing on the city's new bike-sharing program. Starting in September, three hundred bicycles will be available at thirty stations across downtown. Residents can rent a bike for two dollars per half hour, using the mobile app. We chose locations near subway stations and universities, so commuters and students can easily connect with other transportation. Later in the year, we plan to add electric bikes if the first phase goes well. Now I'll take your questions.

In business news, the Daily Ledger has announced that it will stop printing its weekday edition and move entirely online by the end of the year. The newspaper's editor said that declining advertising income and rising paper costs made the change necessary. About forty printing staff will be offered new positions in the digital department or help finding other jobs. The Sunday edition will continue, with a bigger magazine section. Readers who hold print subscriptions will receive a discount on the digital version.

Thanks for coming, everyone. I want to go over the results of our spring campaign. Overall, website visits increased by thirty percent, which is better than we predicted. However, online sales rose by only five percent. Our analysis shows that many visitors left the site at the payment stage. So for the summer campaign, we'll simplify the checkout process and add more payment options. Raj will lead this project, and I'd like each of you to send him your ideas by next Monday.

This is the Drive-Time traffic update. Traffic on Route 9 is moving slowly this morning because of an overturned truck near exit 14. Two lanes are blocked, and police expect clearance work to take at least an hour. Drivers heading downtown are advised to use Maple Avenue instead, although it's busy as well. Buses on the Blue line are running about fifteen minutes behind schedule. On a brighter note, the airport shuttle is running normally. Stay tuned for the next update in thirty minutes.

Good afternoon. As you know, our company was targeted by a phishing email last week. Fortunately, no data was lost, but IT has decided to strengthen our security. Beginning Monday, everyone must change their password every ninety days and use a second verification step, such as a code sent to a phone. Employees who work from home will also need to connect through the company's secure network. If you're not sure how to set up the extra step, the help desk will offer short workshops tomorrow at ten and two.

Welcome to the annual Digital Media Conference. This year, we have more than eight hundred attendees from thirty countries. This morning's keynote speaker, Laura Mendes, is the founder of a podcast network that now reaches five million listeners. After her talk, there will be a short break, and then you can choose among three workshops: video editing, audio production, and social media strategy. Lunch will be served in the garden, but if it rains, we'll move it into the main hall. Please wear your name badge at all times.

Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen, this is your captain speaking. We've reached our cruising altitude of thirty-six thousand feet, and we expect to land in Toronto about ten minutes ahead of schedule, at four fifty p.m. The weather there is cool and cloudy, with a temperature of eleven degrees. The flight attendants will be serving a light meal shortly. Please keep your seat belts fastened whenever you are seated, as we may experience some turbulence over the mountains. Thank you for flying with Northern Air.
